# Write the polyglot file. 
# Structure:
#   - C++ section: #include, #define main int main, fib(), main()  [g++ sees this]
#   - Rust section: use std::env; fn fib() fn main()               [rustc sees this]
# The C++ section is hidden from rustc via a block comment /* ... */
# The Rust section is hidden from g++ via... the problem.
#
# Best achievable: make BOTH sides self-contained.
# C++ side: complete program (compiles + runs correctly)
# Rust side: complete program (compiles + runs correctly)  
# They cant share code, so each has its own fib.
#
# The trick: use #line directives and block comments to make each side
# see ONLY its own code.

# Actually, the cleanest approach that WORKS for C++:
# Put the C++ code in a /* ... */ block comment that rustc skips,
# and put the Rust code after it.
# Problem: g++ sees the Rust code after the comment.
# 
# Solution: make the Rust code ALSO a valid C++ comment continuation
# by ending the file with an open /* that g++ never closes.
# But rustc would see an unterminated comment.
#
# The ONLY working structure I found:
#   C++ code (visible to g++, hidden from rustc via /* ... */)
#   Rust code (visible to rustc, hid
